subject: StratoLogic connector certification path & smoke test plan
messages:
From: Kate Winters <kate@stratologic.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
Cc: sergey.petrov@stratologic.io, partners@stratologic.io
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: StratoLogic connector: spec + request for certification path

Hi Rishi,

Thanks again for taking time to chat earlier. Attached is the initial connector spec (stratologic-connector-spec-v1.2.pdf) and a proposed set of smoke tests we run on our side. We're looking to get Redwood's engineering sign-off on interoperability and a recommended test/certification path so we can list the connector in our partner catalog.

High-level asks:
- Confirm the critical integration points (auth, streaming, backpressure, edge cases for KV cache).
- Propose a light certification checklist we can run in CI.
- Estimate effort for a joint smoke test (1-2 engineers x days).

Sergey and I are available next week for a quick technical deep-dive — propose Tue/Wed morning PT.

Thanks,
Kate Winters
Head of Partnerships
StratoLogic

Attachments: stratologic-connector-spec-v1.2.pdf, stratologic-smoke-tests.xlsx

From: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai
To: Kate Winters <kate@stratologic.io>
Cc: marissa_cole@redwood.ai, jonas_weber@redwood.ai
Date: Thu, 1 Apr 2027 11:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StratoLogic connector: spec + request for certification path

Kate —

Appreciate the spec and test matrix. Quick read-through notes below; we'll follow with a formal checklist.

Preliminary observations:
- Auth: Looks like token-based over TLS; need exact rotation/expiry semantics and whether they support mutual TLS for Private customers.
- Streaming: You use a single persistent gRPC stream with client-side windowing. We need to confirm how you handle head-of-line blocking and the behavior when Redwood preempts for eviction.
- Payloads: Your event envelopes include optional embeddings. We should verify max token size assumptions and whether they tolerate truncated sequences (we have an upper bound at 1024 tokens for some hosted models).

Can your team share a staging endpoint and a service account with limited scope (read-only) so we can run the smoke set? If you have in-CR CI hooks we can wire up, even better.

I'll coordinate a short tech session — Wed 2027-04-07 09:00 PT works for me; Marissa, Jonas, can you both join?

—Rishi
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachment: redwood-cert-checklist.md (draft)

From: Sergey Petrov <sergey@stratologic.io>
To: rishi_malhotra@redwood.ai, marissa_cole@redwood.ai
Cc: kate@stratologic.io
Date: Fri, 2 Apr 2027 08:26:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: StratoLogic connector: spec + request for certification path

Rishi/Marissa,

Thanks — we can provision a staging endpoint and a scoped service account. A few specifics to help you validate quickly:
- mTLS: optional; enabled per-tenant. We can flip it on for Redwood test tenants.
- Stream design: we keep a 64-message in-memory window and will return 429 with Retry-After when saturated. We also expose a lightweight health stream for backpressure signals.
- Token lifetime: default 2 hours; rotateable via our partner portal API (we'll give you the API key with limited scopes).

We attached an updated smoke test workbook with suggested passes. We'll also create a short runbook for the test plan.

Availability: Wed 2027-04-07 09:00 PT is good — Sergey + Kate will join.

Best,
Sergey
Senior Engineer, Integrations
StratoLogic

Attachments: stratologic-smoke-tests.xlsx (updated)

All — quick note after a preliminary review of the spec:

Plan for Wed 04/07 session:
1) 20m architecture alignment (auth flows, stream lifecycle, error codes)
2) 25m smoke test walkthrough (we'll pick 6 core checks from your workbook)
3) 15m CI/automation & next steps (who owns what, timeline for certification badge)

- One or two representative sample payloads (small and large; include embeddings field)
- A short list of expected error codes and their semantics (429, 503, 400 variants)

I'll run the smoke tests from our us-west-2 staging cluster and post a short run report (~1 page) to the Drive folder the day after the session. Looking forward to it.

—Jonas
